findings.title: Materials' 65-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at a forward P/E of 16.01 at percentile 18 while its trailing P/E sits at 34.24 at percentile 83. The market is pricing in 114 percent earnings growth, a bet that would reverse the sector's recent margin pressure, not extend it.

findings.title: Energy's month-long slide contradicts its percentile
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E of 11.89 is at percentile 44, but it has fallen 18 percentile points in a month while its trailing P/E remains rich at percentile 82. Analysts are slashing forward estimates faster than reported earnings are deteriorating, leaving the sector's cheapness suspect.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward multiple defies its percentile
findings.body: Real Estate's forward P/E of 33.81 sits at percentile 7, yet it has dropped 32 percentile points in a month and implies a 4 percent earnings decline. The multiple is historically cheap only because estimates have been cut so aggressively that the denominator is collapsing.
